newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HUNDREDS GATHER IN THREDBO TO PRAY FOR LANDSLIDE VICTIMS
Hundreds of people have gathered for a special ecumenical service offering prayers to the friends and families of those killed and missing in the Thredbo landslide.
Twenty people were trapped when the landslide caused the collapse of two ski lodges in the alpine resort, in New South Wales, just before midnight last Wednesday.
So far nine people have been confirmed dead, 10 are still missing, and one - Stuart Diver - has been recovered alive, after over 60 hours trapped in the rubble.

Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer, Opposition leader Kim Beazley and Governor General Sir William Deane, have joined church leaders, the local community, and families and friends of those missing or dead, to show their support and sympathy.
The service also paid tribute to Mr Diver, who was rescued from the rubble two days ago.
At the service, Sir William praised the support of rescue teams and the Snowy Mountains community.

"We are sure that the Snowy Mountains and its people - which hold such a special place in our nation, in its achievements, and in its folklore - will come through these tragic days with their legendary determination and courage," Sir William said.
Sir William also read a message of sympathy from the Queen, and handed the families of the victims a lighted candle, a symbol of the nation's caring.
He spoke of his admiration for the skill and bravery of the rescue crews, still working around-the-clock to try to free those unaccounted for.
Speaking in Thredbo, Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer also praised the rescue workers, and told of his confidence that the community would "bounce back" from the tragedy.
On his way to the ski resort for the service, Mr Fischer visited Mr Diver, who he said is making a rapid recovery from the injuries he suffered during his ordeal, including frostbitten toes.

"He particularly wanted to make the point that he could move his toes, he could feel those toes moving...and he wanted to pass on to everyone at the site of the rescue his great thanks," Mr Fischer said.
SCHOOLS TO FACE BURDEN OF MORE STUDENTS
Schools will have to adjust to the needs of young people returning to education because they can no longer get unemployment benefits, according to Federal Schools Minister David Kemp.
The Opposition said a leaked Cabinet submission shows around $140 million should be spent to give schools extra resources to cope with extra students.
Shadow Education Minister Mark Latham said the Government should adopt the spending proposals at tomorrow's Cabinet meeting on unemployment.
Dr Kemp would not comment on the submission but said the Government had already committed substantial extra resources for schools.

"Schools will have to adjust to any particular needs that these students have and that's why the Government is putting additional resources into school-based apprenticeships and encouraging young people to go on with training that will lead them into careers and jobs," Dr Kemp said.
JEWELLERY MURDER ACCUSED "LIED AT SCENE OF CRIME"
A Melbourne court has heard a man charged with murdering a city jeweller and his son lied to police when they found him at the murder scene.
Manuel Adajian, 41, is charged with the murders of 49-year-old jeweller Lean Thoeun Pin and his 21-year-old son, Virayuth in December last year.
Crown Prosecutor Jeremy Rapke told the court Mr Adajian had debts totalling more than $500,000 including about $23,000 owed to the Pin family.
Mr Rapke alleged Mr Adajian went to the Pin's jewellery business in Swanston Street and demanded they open a safe, threatening them with a heavy calibre military-style pistol.
Mr Adajian allegedly shot Mr Pin and his son three times each killing them both, and shot Mr Pin's wife twice as well as striking her 12 times in the head with the butt of the pistol.
Unable to unlock the door and escape, he was allegedly still at the scene when police arrived.
The prosecution told the court Mr Adajian had told police he had been knocked unconscious when two Asian men pinched him on the back of the neck, an assertion the prosecutors described as a lie.
The hearing is continuing.
CSIRO TRIALLING GENE TREATMENT FOR HIV
Australia's first clinical trial of a possible gene treatment for the virus which causes AIDS is underway.
The trial is based on the CSIRO's "gene shears" technology, and involves six pairs of identical twins, of whom one of each pair is HIV-positive.
Chief Executive of Gene Shears Pty Ltd Dr Leigh Farrell said the new process involved previous research into plant enzymes called ribozymes.
"It was found that these ribozymes were involved in the actual replication of the virus, the reproduction of it," Dr Farrell said.

"Scientists at CSIRO discovered that you could take the engine out of that enzymne...and then cause it to destroy other RNA selectively...It's really like genetic scissors that have surgical precision at knocking out the function of a gene," he said.
Dr Farrell said each infected twin will receive anti-HIV blood cells, but it will be some time before they can be sure the process will work.
"We're asking the questions firstly - is the therapy safe? And secondly - does the ribozyme gene improve the survival of the T-cell, relative to the control cells that we've also put in," he said.
"We'll get some indication within six months, of whether our potential treatment has worked. Within 12 months, we'll get the full results."
QLD POLICE OFFICER SHOT WITH HIS OWN GUN
Queensland police say a post-mortem examination has shown a detective who died during an operational raid last night was shot with his own service revolver.
Police are still treating the incident as a homicide - but are not ruling out an accident.
Detective Sergeant Leonard Hooper had been part of a raid on an inner-city Brisbane unit when the shooting happened.
He had been at the rear of the unit when his colleagues heard the gunshot. Sgt Hooper died in hospital a short time later.
Sgt Hooper's gun is being tested to determine if there were any other fingerprints on the weapon.
Police Commissioner Jim O'Sullivan said Sgt Hooper's death was a great loss for the police service in Queensland, but said his family will be looked after.
